sections.name: File setup, ScoringBucket
sections.title: File setup and target role type
sections.what: States the file's purpose, imports the profile and model settings types, and defines one target role bucket with an id, name, and description.
sections.why: The buckets are shared with the scoring route, so this type keeps them consistent.

sections.name: scoreJobWithAI
sections.title: Sending a job for scoring
sections.what: Sends one job to the server for scoring and returns the result. For the together provider, the key is not forwarded, so the server's default is used instead.
sections.why: Likely reason: the server holds a default key for the together provider, so the browser does not need to send one.
sections.watch_out: The function takes many positional arguments that are easy to swap, and it does not check that the buckets list is non-empty.

summary: Browser-side helper that sends one job posting and the candidate profile to the server route that scores it with AI, then returns the scored result.
purpose: Lets the pages request a job score without running the AI call in the browser.
why: Likely reason: keeping AI calls on the server protects the provider key and avoids browser limits. This file is the browser side of that split.
how: Reads the saved model settings. Packs the job text, company, role, location, seniority, sector, remote flag, target role buckets, profile, and provider settings into one request. Sends it to the scoring route, then returns the parsed result or throws an error with the server's message.
inputs: Job description text, company, role, location, seniority, sector, remote flag, the list of target role buckets, the candidate profile, and the model settings saved in the browser.
outputs: The parsed scoring result from the server, or an error with a readable message.
risks: The header comment says the key stays on the server, but for providers other than together the request body includes the API key from local settings. The key therefore travels from the browser to the server. Error text from the server is shown directly. The long list of positional arguments is easy to mix up.
debug: If scoring fails, check the request to the scoring route and its status code in the browser's network view. Confirm the model settings contain a provider and a key. A message that only says Scoring failed with a status number means the server returned no details, so check the server route.
